name: Iowa Custom Wood Company, LLC
old_description: Very friendly and willing to work with me so my design came out perfect! All I needed was someone to carve a design I had made on a CNC, but Andrew was more than willing to offer some advice to produce a better outcome! I will be going again when I have another design ready!
about:
Iowa Custom Wood Company, LLC operates from Williamsburg, Iowa, where it was founded in 2009 by craftsman Andy (also referred to as Andrew). The shop began with a focus on custom woodworking, building one-off pieces for local clients and gradually expanding its capabilities to include CNC routing and digital design.

The company produces custom cabinetry, furniture, and specialty projects such as live-edge tables, epoxy river tables, kitchen islands, and architectural millwork. Its 48-by-120-inch AVID CNC router, driven by Fusion 360 CAD/CAM, handles panel processing, sign carving, and complex joinery, while a SawStop table saw and traditional hand tools support bench-side assembly. Finishes range from sprayed film coatings to hand-rubbed oils and hard waxes. All lumber is kiln-dried and sourced from select sawmills.

Primary customers are residential homeowners seeking kitchen remodels, built-ins, and heirloom furniture; the shop has also completed a full interior rebuild of a 100-year-old passenger rail car. Daycare operators, gift buyers, and repeat clients round out the base, with projects often starting from a sketch or 3D model developed in collaboration with the client.

The founder emphasizes generational durability through traditional joinery, safe shop practices, and a design-first workflow that lets customers preview projects in 3D before cutting begins. The mission centers on delivering functional quality rather than volume, keeping each piece a one-off collaboration.

name: Iron Works
old_description: Since 2003, Robert and John Klerlein have grown a successful enterprise that is the area’s top structural and miscellaneous steel fabricator and erector. Located in Milton, DE, Iron Works is your one stop shop for any steel construction project.
about:
Iron Works is a structural and miscellaneous steel fabricator and erector based in Milton, Delaware. Founded in 2003 by brothers Robert and John Klerlein, the family-owned business draws on over 70 years of combined experience between the two owners. The company began as a one-stop shop for steel construction projects in the region.

The shop handles simple to complex fabrication, including plate burning, and produces full steel packages such as stairs, rails, ladders, and ornamental metalwork. Annual output ranges from 1,800 to 2,400 tons of steel. The operation also provides complete steel erection services, delivering projects from start to finish.

Iron Works serves the construction industry, with completed projects including the Dogfish Head Brew Pub, the Grifasi Office Building, and the Movies at Midway Cube Theater. Its customer base spans commercial, hospitality, and entertainment construction projects.

The owners emphasize a hands-on approach and precision in every phase, aiming to keep multiple projects on schedule through attention to detail. The business was built to make the steel construction process as smooth and efficient as possible for clients.

name: Ironwood Plastics Inc.
old_description: Since 1979, Ironwood Plastics has been a leader in the plastics industry. Founded by Gordon K. Stephens, the company was sold to CTB, Inc., a Berkshire Hathaway Company, in 2010.  We recognize that technology is constantly changing and our state-of-the-art facilities in Ironwood, Michigan and Two Rivers, Wisconsin enable us to stay ahead of the latest trends and technologies, giving our clients the highest quality products to meet their unique specifications.
about:
Ironwood Plastics Inc. was founded in 1979 by Gordon K. Stephens in Ironwood, Michigan. The company was acquired by CTB, Inc., a Berkshire Hathaway subsidiary, in 2010 and operates today as a division of that organization. A second production site was established in Two Rivers, Wisconsin, giving the company a dual-facility footprint in the Upper Midwest.

The company specializes in custom injection molding with a focus on complex, high-precision processes. Its core capabilities include two-shot molding, reel-to-reel molding, insert molding, close-tolerance molding, and overmolding. A scientific, data-driven approach to process development and optimization underpins production, and secondary services such as pad printing, sonic welding, and tape-and-reel packaging provide a single-source solution. The management team brings more than 200 years of combined plastics-industry experience.

Primary markets served are automotive, electronics, and medical. Automotive projects have included HVAC damper components, fuel-pressure sensors, cylinder-deactivation valves, and inlet check valves for plastic fuel tanks. Electronics work centers on reel-to-reel insert-molded connectors and sensor components requiring zero-defect quality. Medical applications are referenced in the context of tight-tolerance molding for critical devices.

Ironwood's stated vision since inception has been "to be a world class injection molder of complex projects." The company differentiates itself through its engineering-driven methodology, investment in in-line inspection and vision-assisted automation, and a partnership model that emphasizes traceability from resin receipt through finished product.

name: Isoflex Packaging
old_description: , is a manufacturer of specialty films for the laminating, printing, coating and converting markets. What started in 1985 as an idea to build a company that paved a new way of doing things in the film industry has grown into a major film manufacturer that operates seven locations throughout the U.S. We deliver custom-engineered solutions to solve the toughest flexible packaging challenges.
about:
Isoflex Packaging, headquartered in Vancouver, Washington, was founded in 1985 with the goal of introducing a new approach to the film industry. The company is minority-owned (NMSDC certified) and operates as a privately-held business.

The company produces specialty films for laminating, printing, coating, and converting markets. Its seven U.S. facilities run 24/7/365 on monolayer, three-, five-, and seven-layer co-extrusion lines, delivering a combined film and bag capacity of 350 million pounds per year. Core capabilities include high-performance barrier films, shrink films, custom bags, auto-insert packaging, non-shrink sheeting, and stretch hood films.

Isoflex serves food and beverage, consumer goods, institutional, industrial, agricultural, and medical/pharmaceutical sectors. Customers include converters, printers, and packagers seeking custom-engineered flexible packaging solutions.

Founded to pioneer a different way of making films, Isoflex emphasizes custom-engineered solutions for difficult packaging challenges. The company highlights sustainable manufacturing, offering How2Recycle®-labeled, post-consumer recycled, bio-based, compostable, and antimicrobial film options.

name: J & C Wood Products
old_description: Our new website is optimized for the most current web browsing technology. If you are using an older web browser, part of our website may not function properly as designed. Please consider upgrading your browser for an error free experience.
about:
J & C Wood Products operates from Plaucheville, Louisiana, a town of roughly 288 residents. The company was founded in 2001 by Jody and Candace Chenevert, who brought over 25 years of hardwood industry experience to the venture. Starting from humble beginnings, the couple built a business focused on reclaimed and specialty wood products.

The company mills solid wood flooring from reclaimed antique heart pine, white oak, hickory/pecan, and hemlock, as well as producing beams, table tops, counter tops, stair treads, mantles, doors, cabinets, charcuterie boards, and pre-finished engineered flooring. A key process is thermally modified kiln drying, where wood is heated above 180°C in an oxygen-free environment for up to five days to enhance durability without chemicals. Reclaimed beams are sourced from antique structures across the United States and milled to custom dimensions. The operation includes a showroom at its new mill facility.

J & C serves both commercial and residential markets, supplying flooring and beams to homeowners, builders, and designers. Its products have been featured in Design & Build Magazine of Southwest Louisiana, and customer testimonials reference projects in Arkansas, Louisiana, and New Orleans. The company also provides installation services through its own crews.

The Cheneverts emphasize old-world craftsmanship, positioning their La Olden brand as ultra-premium unfinished flooring made in the traditions of traditional artisans. The thermally modified wood line is promoted as a sustainable, chemical-free option for outdoor applications with a lifespan of 25 to 50 years.

old_description: J Custom Supply, Inc. is a local Louisiana company with an international reach.  We have supported the electrical needs of theater, entertainment and emergency portable power industries for over forty years. The list of our customers range from local bands and entertainment venues to major convention centers across the country and large generator rental companies.  Our customer list includes such famous names as Boeing, Feld Entertainment, Caterpillar, BAE Systems and Mercedes-Benz.  We have customers in almost every US state and Puerto Rico.  Our international customers include Canada, Arabia, Korea, Hong Kong, Great Britain, Taiwan, India, Singapore and the Bahamas, to name just a few.
about:
J Custom Supply, Inc. was founded in 1979 in Zachary, Louisiana, by Jason Fendelson to provide stage lighting and power distribution equipment for the touring production Holiday on Ice. The company relocated to Baton Rouge in 2005 when Fendelson retired and Charles "Gil" Gilliam assumed ownership.

The company stocks and supplies a broad range of cam-style connectors, including Crouse-Hinds Cam-Lok and Marinco CAM Technology lines, along with generator connection boxes, test clamps, and front-of-house power panels. It maintains one of the largest inventories of cam connectors in the southeastern United States, with most items available for immediate shipment.

J Custom Supply serves the theater, entertainment, and emergency portable power sectors. Its customer base spans local bands and venues to major convention centers and generator rental firms across nearly every U.S. state and Puerto Rico, with international clients in Canada, Saudi Arabia, Korea, Hong Kong, the United Kingdom, Taiwan, India, Singapore, and the Bahamas. Notable accounts include Boeing, Feld Entertainment, Caterpillar, BAE Systems, and Mercedes-Benz.

The business was created to meet the specialized power distribution demands of touring ice shows and has since expanded its inventory depth and geographic reach to support a wide range of live-event and temporary-power applications.

about:
JM Cooper Co., Inc. has operated from Middletown, Rhode Island since its founding in 1925. The company began as a sheet metal fabrication and installation shop and remains a second-generation family business led by George Oliveira and his son David, who oversee daily operations.

The shop focuses on residential and light commercial sheet metal work, offering fabrication and installation services that span HVAC systems, historical replicas, CNC machining, and custom copper detailing. Projects are handled on a job-by-job basis with an emphasis on getting the work done right the first time, and the team works directly with contractors to meet exacting field conditions.

Customers include area builders and contractors such as Downes Building Company Inc. and K&R Construction LLC, who have relied on the firm for two decades for flashing details, copper fabrications, and other architectural metalwork. The company serves the residential construction and light commercial construction sectors primarily in the Newport County region.

The firm distinguishes itself through meticulous attention to detail, artistic ability in designing complicated flashing details, and a reputation for timely, professional service. The "done right the first time" philosophy has guided its approach for nearly a century, with an emphasis on responsive communication and on-site problem solving.

name: J M Industries
old_description: JMI have been servicing the machines we sell for over 40 years. We refurbish the machines and test them to ensure they are fully operational prior to shipment. If you buy a machine from JMI, odds are good we can still service it many years later, even if the OEM won’t. We do not typically charge for evaluation.
about:
J M Industries, based in North Billerica, Massachusetts, has been servicing semiconductor manufacturing equipment since its founding in 1982. The company began as a service and refurbishment operation for the machines it sells, and over four decades has built a reputation for keeping equipment operational long after original manufacturers discontinue support.

The company refurbishes and resells a broad range of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, including thermal shock chambers, mask aligners, wire bonders, ball bonders, probers, and reflow systems. It also specializes in rebuilding vacuum pumps, blowers, and dry pumps, offering a 2‑3 week turnaround on rebuilds. J M Industries maintains one of the largest and most diversified inventories of refurbished semiconductor equipment worldwide, with over 300 dual‑stage direct‑drive pumps in stock. Technicians perform upgrades such as touch‑screen retrofits for Mech‑el and MEI wire bonders and complete SST electronics rebuilds with a one‑year warranty.

Customers include semiconductor fabs and assembly houses that need cost‑effective alternatives to new equipment purchases. The company supports equipment from brands such as Blue M, Technics, Perkin Elmer, Mechel, Karl Suss, Laurier, Ewald, Thermo/Neslab, YES, EG, Loomis, Mech‑el, and MEI. Its vacuum pump rebuilding service serves any operation relying on vacuum technology, while its equipment upgrades extend the life of legacy wire bonders and aligners.

J M Industries differentiates itself by offering long‑term support even after OEMs stop providing parts or service, and by not charging for equipment evaluations. The company contrasts its model with auctioneers and brokers, emphasizing that its refurbished machines come with a substantive warranty rather than a 'taillight' guarantee, and that it avoids buyer premiums and forced carrier choices.

name: J M Mold South Inc
old_description: We’ve been refining this idea since 1986, when David M. Bowers founded the company as JM Mold South. In 2008, Dave’s son and daughter joined senior management — David M. Bowers II became CEO and Michelle Powell became COO.
about:
J M Mold South Inc., doing business as JMMS, was founded in 1986 by David M. Bowers in Easley, South Carolina. The family-owned company transitioned to second-generation leadership in 2008 when Bowers' son, David M. Bowers II, became chief executive officer and his daughter, Michelle Powell, became chief operating officer. The firm maintains its headquarters in Easley and operates engineering and tool-making facilities in Dong Guan, China.

JMMS provides total program management for die casting and injection molding tooling, covering thermoplastic injection molding, thermoset injection and compression/transfer molding, and die cast tooling. Its services span design validation, concurrent engineering, Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), project management, troubleshooting, and mold maintenance. The company uses a Cimatron 13.0 CAD/CAM platform to integrate communications, collaboration, and program management across its global operations.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers and Tier vendors in the automotive, medical technology, and consumer products sectors. In consumer products, JMMS has produced molded components for microwaves, mixers, blenders, refrigerators, icemakers, and air deflection systems. A 2016 partnership with the Moldetipo Group expanded its reach into the global automotive market.

JMMS emphasizes single-source accountability, combining design, engineering, manufacturing, and maintenance under one roof. The company states that its next-generation tooling approach delivers standardized, repeatable processes that meet OEM quality benchmarks and lead times while lowering total cost of ownership, backed by an ISO 9001:2015 registered quality management system.
